label: real-analysis
tail:
A1 and A2 are complete for the wave-5 `real-analysis` batch. Three files written, no item file touched.

## What I found

**No fatal defect.** All 31 items, all 211 proof steps, and every dependency citation were read against the on-disk text of the 60 external targets. Zero undeclared dependencies, zero dangling fact/step references, all 21 source URLs return 200.

**A1 — provenance** (`wave5-real-analysis.provenance.jsonl`, 31 rows): 15 `literature-derived`/`exact-source`, 13 `ai-altered`/`semantic-source`, 3 `ai-generated`/`trivial`. No `established-knowledge` rows, so **no Alpha URL waiver is needed anywhere in this batch**. None of the 31 items carries a legacy `authorship` line, so the A4 retag is purely additive and voids no judge stamp.

The three `ai-generated` calls are the bespoke witnesses (`x_{k+1}=(x_k+1)/3`; the interleaving `1,1,2,1,3,…`; `x_{k+1}=x_k+1/x_k`), each tagged on the witness per the wave-0 precedent, each with the truth verification written out, and each with **zero `deps` consumers corpus-wide** — so the label is mechanically inert either way. I escalated all three as borderline. Conversely I kept `fs-convergent-subsequence-implies-bounded` at `statement: ai-altered` deliberately: it *is* a `deps` target, so the statement label has to classify the sourced refuted claim, not the local witness.

`def-interval` — 338 consumers, the most load-bearing item in either wave — came out `ai-altered`, so every topology batch citing it stays legal.

**A2 — proof contracts** (`wave5-real-analysis.proof-contracts.json`): 26 items, 322 citation contracts, 211 step contracts, 208 boundary dispositions. `proof-contract.mjs --strict` reports **3 errors, 0 warnings** — every quote verified verbatim in the named section, every step mapped exactly once.

Those 3 errors are one real finding: `ex-nested-intervals-single-point [L8]` and `cex-nested-open-intervals-empty [L5]` are declared facts that **no proof step consumes**. I recorded them honestly with `uses: []` rather than omitting them. Nonfatal; I recommend no repair and costed the alternative for Alpha.

Five other nonfatal observations, all with "no repair" recommended and reasons given — the sharpest is **N1**: `thm-cauchy-criterion-via-lub`'s title generalises to *every complete ordered field*, while its three cited lemmas are all stated for `ℝ` through `def-real-limit`'s rational-ε convention. The claim is true and standard; it just isn't discharged inline. And **N6**, corpus-wide rather than batch-local: 24 of 31 items pair a Rudin theorem citation with the Wikipedia article *about the book*, and five pair Bartle & Sherbert §3.5 with an unrelated page. I located open-access sources carrying the actual clauses (PlanetMath, ProofWiki, MIT OCW) and put them in the ledger.

Next action is A3: Alpha adjudicates, then the bulk pure-retag pass at A4 under a single stage snapshot.
